title: Blue Star Museums
description: As part of the Blue Star Museums program, the San Diego Archaeological Center offers free admission to active-duty military personnel and their families from Armed Forces Day through Labor Day. The free admission program is available for those currently serving in the United States Military–Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, Coast Guard–including Reservists, National Guardsman (regardless of status), U.S. Public Health Commissioned Corps, NOAA Commissioned Corps, and up to five family members. The military ID holder can be either active duty service member or other dependent family member with the appropriate ID card. The active duty member does not have to be present for family members to use the program. Just bring your DD Form 1173 ID Card, or DD Form 1173-1 ID Card, for active duty military family members. About Blue Star Museums: Blue Star Museums is a collaboration among the National Endowment for the Arts, Blue Star Families, the Department of War, and museums across America to offer free admission to the nation’s active duty military personnel including National Guard and Reserve and their families each summer. The program begins on Armed Forces Day in mid-May and ends on Labor Day at the beginning of September. For more information, including a full list of participating museums, visit the Blue Star Families website .
location: San Diego Archaeological Center, 16666 San Pasqual Valley Road, Escondido, CA

Happy Hour Cheers: Finish your adventure with a refreshing drink at Novo Brewing, with non-alcoholic options available too—a great way to toast to community and conservation. title: Nat at Night
description: On Fridays, the San Diego Natural History Museum is open until 11 PM just for you. Enjoy access to all open exhibitions and our rooftop deck for good views and great vibes. The rooftop is open to all visitors and serves beer, wine, non-alcoholic drinks , and food from Wolf in the Woods. Take a selfie with a megalodon shark, see scientists at work in our Paleo Center , admire glittering gems, get a close up look at spiders and snakes, and so much more. Best of all, get a look at our brand-new exhibition, Washed Ashore: Art to Save the Sea and grab a drink in the dive bar while chatting with a scientist. On select dates, channel your inner artist with Sketchparty , get competitive during trivia, or unwind while listening to the rooftop DJ. Hungry for more? The Craft Taco , located inside the Atrium, is a vibrant taco restaurant offering a delectable fusion of flavors and artisanal creations. They offer made-to-order tacos featuring signature blue corn tortillas, delectable burritos and bowls, and a variety of drinks and coffees. Admission is half-price after 5 PM, and parking is free after 6 PM. You can buy your tickets online in advance or buy them at the door the night of . title: LIONS, COYOTES & BOBCATS, OH MY!  & one more… GRAY FOX!
partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
description: Linda Hawley's Nature Adventures! Ages 4-10 with an adult San Diego’s top predators & largest mammals: How do they differ? What do they eat? Where are their habitats? How do we co-exist with them? How do we help them? How do they help us? ABOUT THE PRESENTER: Linda Hawley, Ed.M., delights children & adults alike with the animated enthusiasm she brings to her monthly programs by entertaining them with her PowerPoint presentation, songs, puppets, real animal pelts & nests, replicated skulls, specimens, scats & tracks; take-home craft materials &/or handouts will be provided. EVERYONE HAS FUN LEARNING! Ms. Hawley has 40+ years of experience as a classroom teacher, college professor, naturalist guide & educator for Audubon Society’s OutdoorExplore! & at Mission Trails Regional Park, where she created & taught her “wildly popular” nature classes for 10 years. She is author of NATURE ADVENTURES! A Guidebook of Nature Facts, Songs and Hikes in San Diego County, Sunbelt Publications, Inc. 2017 Her classes go full STEAM ahead: S—Sciences—zoology, biology, botany T—Technology—PowerPoint, Smartphone, computers E—English language, new vocabulary, scientific terms A—Arts, crafts, creativity M—Music—Singing about the fauna of San Diego
location: Grant Park, 2310 Camino Del Rio N., San Diego, CA

title: Tech Help 2.0
description: Learn how to use your smart phone, tablet, laptop and other devices. Get help with internet searching, email, downloading apps, eBooks, and more. Sign-up recommended. Walk-in appointments are now also available.

title: Fixit Clinic
description: Don't toss it; fix it! Join the San Diego Fixit Clinic at the Ramona Community Library on September 20th from 10 AM to 1 PM. Fix your items for free, first come, first served. Learn how to: • Fix broken appliances and gadgets • Repair road and mountain bikes • Mend your favorite outfit Free to the public, register today: https://bit.ly/Ramona-Library

title: Paws and Tales: Read to a SD Humane Society Canine Ambassador
description: Read aloud to a trained Canine Ambassador from the San Diego Humane Society. Program geared toward school aged children. Build confidence and practice reading with a friendly furry friend!

title: Creekside Critters: Interesting Insects
description: Join us for a series of animal programs presented by the San Dieguito River Valley Conservancy! For the month of September, get up close and personal with all manner of insects with artist and entomologist Francisco Basso! Sign up on: https://www.sdrvc.org/events

title: Sweetwater Safari Hike
description: Join us every Saturday as we explore the Sweetwater Marsh Trail on the San Diego Bay National Wildlife Refuge! We will learn about the history of the Sweetwater Marsh, the salt marsh ecosystem, and the plants and wildlife thriving in this protected space. Backpacks with fun activities, including magnifying glasses and binoculars, will be available for families to use while on the hike. Check-in time: 11:30 am Duration: 30-45 Minutes Meeting Location: We will meet outside the front doors of the Living Coast Discovery Center located at 1000 Gunpowder Point Drive, Chula Vista, CA 91910. Driving directions: From the I5 freeway, exit at E street and head west to the Living Coast Discovery Center parking lot. This hike location is located on a wildlife refuge, and all visitors must park in the outer lot and take the free Living Coast Discovery Center shuttle. Suggested parking: This locations parking lot is located outside of a wildlife refuge. All visitors must take the free shuttle from the parking lot located on Gunpowder Point Drive. This lot is located at Gunpowder Point Drive, Chula Vista CA 91910. Restrooms and Water: The nearest restrooms are located inside the front doors of the Living Coast Discovery Center. You do not have to pay to use the restrooms, but if visitors choose to enter the facility to visit exhibits they must pay the admission fees. Hike lengths: This trail is approximately 1 mile in length. Program Supplies: Please make sure to wear comfortable clothes and shoes for hiking. Bringing a water bottle, bug protection, and sun protection are highly recommended. Hiking level: Easy No pets will be allowed on the hike.
location: Living Coast Discovery Center, 1000 Gunpowder Point Drive, Chula Vista, CA 91910

title: Grape Day Festival
description: Join us at the Escondido Grape Day Festival, presented by the Escondido History Center, The Rincon Band of Luiseno Indians, and Brothers of 6 Charities. This year’s event features activities for all ages including grape stomping, live music, children’s activities and games, antique farm equipment, food vendors, local arts and crafts, wine and beer garden, and more. Visit the SDAC’s booth to step into the fascinating world of archaeology. Assemble plate puzzles, and explore historic artifacts from Escondido. This event is hosted by the Escondido History Center and the Brothers of 6. For more information, visit the Escondido Grape Day Festival website .
location: Grape Day Park, 321 N Broadway, Escondido, CA

title: BLOOMING SEEDS SoCal
description: Blooming Seeds Socal:  Providing STEM education to neurodivergent students!  First Saturday of every month! Our mission is to create a nurturing and inclusive environment where every child, regardless of their abilities, can experience the wonder of discovery and the joy of learning.  BLOOMING SEEDS works hard to provide STEM education to neurodivergent students. Join us for the next set of classes at the 4S Ranch Library!

title: Santee Teens Kindness Collective
description: The Santee Teens Kindness Collective is a service club dedicated to giving back to the community through once a month, hands-on projects. First Saturday of the month at 2:00 p.m. For grades 6-12.  Help us give back this month by making early literacy kits for Head Start!

title: Robot Garage
description: Students build and program robots and other electronic projects using microcontrollers, motors and sensors. Students learn basic electronics, soldering, mechanical construction, communication busses, motion control and other aspects of software driven electronic devices. This class is most suitable for students 7th grade and older, and students should have some programming experience.

title: Sensory Friendly Mornings
description: Join us every Sunday from 9:00 a.m. - 10:30 a.m. for early mornings geared for families with children on the spectrum or with sensory sensitivities: Join a welcoming, comfortable environment Enjoy the Museum in a quiet and accepting setting Make connections and share resources with other families Free with Museum admission.
location: Children's Museum of Discovery, 320 North Broadway, Escondido, CA

title: Intro to Robotics (Robot Riot)
description: Build & Code: Micro:Bit Robotics Take your coding skills to the next level by building and programming your own robot! In this exciting hands-on camp, students will use the Micro:Bit microcontroller to bring their creations to life. You'll learn how to program sensors, motors, and LEDs using Python, JavaScript, or block-based coding. Work with friends to design, build, and code robots that can move, interact, and respond to their environment. This camp is perfect for young engineers and programmers who want to explore the world of robotics in a fun and interactive way! All equipment will be provided by The League of AMAZING Programmers. If you would like to keep your robot at the end of the course there will be an additional fee of $55.00 for the starter kit. As we progress through the course there may be optional add ons to the robot that can be purchased through amazon, those are optional and will be communicated if/when your child gets to that point.

title: Senior Monday
description: Come join us for an engaging lecture on fascinating scientific topics, followed by an unforgettable show in the Heikoff Giant Dome Theater—all for the discounted admission of $10! It's a great way to learn something new and connect with others in our community. Plus, enjoy engaging and interactive experiences that you won't want to miss. We can't wait to explore the wonders of science with you! Click here to see the lineup of lecture topics, speakers and documentaries. Tickets are available only at the ticket counter on the day of the event. Fleet Members have free access to the Sharp Minds lecture.
location: Fleet Science Center, 1875 El Prado, San Diego, CA

title: Birding & Brews – Breakfast Edition
description: Be an Ocean Connector and start your day with birding and brews! Sip on smooth, nitro cold brew from Trident Coffee as you learn how their values of connection, community, and character align with our conservation mission. Then, head out on a guided walking tour along the Bayshore Bikeway at South San Diego Bay, equipped with binoculars and field guides. What to Expect: Coffee Tasting: Kick off the tour with a unique nitro cold brew tasting, crafted locally by Trident Coffee. Birdwatching Walk: Explore the Bayshore Bikeway with expert guides to spot native and migratory birds. Ecology & Conservation: Learn about local ecosystems and conservation efforts to protect our coastal wildlife. Best of all, every tour supports our education programs for South Bay youth!
location: San Diego Bay Refuge, 501 Florence St, Imperial Beach, CA

title: BeTween Tuesday
description: Tweens have fun at the library! Program activities can vary from arts and crafts, board games, bingo, and more!   Grades 6-8. First come first serve, supplies are limited and subject to change without notice.

title: Lakeside Kids' Crew: Chess
description: Join us for a fun afternoon of chess, all skill levels welcome. Engage in a game or learn how to play with your library friends.

title: Project NexTech: Natural Sciences Workshop
description: On alternating Tuesdays, we'll have Project NexTech teaching basic engineering and natural science in a fun way!  This week, we'll be exploring natural science concepts through fun hands-on experiments and activities such as making hand sanitizer, dissecting plants, making slime, and more!  No sign-up required; for ages 6-13.

title: Toddler Tales
description:
Welcome to Toddler Storytime, a special program designed for our walkers to age 3 years old! This weekly series focuses on nurturing your toddler's development and social skills through a mix of books, songs, crafts, and guided play.

Each session includes:

♦Story Adventures: Simple, engaging books that capture young imaginations and foster early literacy.

♦Musical Fun: Interactive songs and rhymes that develop language skills and a sense of rhythm.

♦Creative Crafts: Hands-on crafts that encourage creativity and fine motor development.

♦Playtime Activities: Guided play sessions that promote exploration, problem solving, and social interactions.

Join us for Toddler Storytime, where your child can grow, learn, and make new friends in a fun and supportive environment!

title: Tinker Tuesday: Aluminum Foil Boat Challenge
description:
Let's learn about buoyancy by experimenting with aluminum foil! Build an aluminum foil boat and see how many marbles it can hold before it sinks.

Tinker Tuesday is a hands-on educational program that allows children to explore, create, design, and problem solve focusing on STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Math) concepts.

title: Habitat Restoration | Nature Collective | San Elijo Lagoon
description: Join Nature Collective for hands-on fun to help improve coastal sage scrub habitats for plants + animals indigenous to the area.

title: Teddy Bear Picnic
description: Bring your favorite stuffy for a Teddy Bear Picnic at the Museum! On Wednesday, September 9th, from 10 a.m. - 12 p.m., families will enjoy special themed activities, including: Teddy Bear Picnic Sing-Along Special Storytime Scavenger Hunt Special Craft We encourage families to bring their picnic blanket and snacks* for a fun-filled morning! *We are a peanut-free facility. All snacks must be peanut-free.
location: Children's Museum of Discovery, 320 North Broadway, Escondido, CA

title: Pre-K Play
description: Bring your littles to meet and have fun! The library will provide toys and a play space for kids to play together and socialize. For ages 0-5. Parent/caregiver supervision required.

title: Brick Builders
description: Use your imagination to complete a brick building challenge with Lego bricks or build whatever you'd like! Hosted in partnership with the City of Imperial Beach Parks, Recreation, and Community Services department. For ages 6-12.

title: Teens Create: Hydro-Dipped Notebooks
description:
Construct, craft, and create at our twice-monthly S.T.E.A.M. activity for teens! This in-person program takes place on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of the month at 3:30 pm.

Today's Activity: Hydro-Dipped Notebooks. Use marbling paints and water surface tension to create a unique design on the cover of a notebook.

Snacks provided!

For students in 6th-12th grade. Program made possible by the Bette Sherman Fund.

title: Baby Sensory Play Time
description: Join us for a special program designed for babies and their caregivers to explore sights, sounds, and textures in a safe and friendly environment. Develop early motor skills and engage their senses through fun activities every other week.

title: Little Explorers: Pumpkin Play
description:
Come join the Library every second Thursday at 11am! Little Explorers will provide hands on activities to promote early childhood development and sensory skills. Geared towards babies- 4 years old with a parent or caregiver. No registration required.

This month.... it's time for pumpkin play! Your child will get a slice of pumpkin to explore with all five of their senses, baby wipes will be provided!

title: Mobile Recreation
description: Enjoy some fresh air, exercise, and activities at Veteran's Park with the City of Imperial Beach Parks, Recreation, and Community Services department and the department of US Fish & Wildlife. For all ages. Monthly, every 2nd Thursday of the month.

title: LEGO Builders Club
description: LEGO Builders Club is held on the second Thursday of the month from 3:30PM to 4:30PM. Recommended for 5 and up, participants will focus on monthly themes and will present their design the last 10-15 minutes of the program.

title: KITS FOR KINDNESS
description: Hygiene Kit Workshop Learn why hygiene access matters and help create hygiene kits for those who need it. Earn volunteer hours as well! For kids & families! Healthcare isn't a privilege, it's a right.

title: Come meet the REACH Program
description:
Landes REACH Open House!

Meet Reach staff and learn more about Project REACH, an after-school program for teens!

Food and resources will be provided for families in attendance.

5:00-6:30 - Resources & food

6:30 - Program presentation

title: Fizz & Ferment: The Art of Kombucha
description:
Fizz, flavor, and a little fermentation magic! Join UC Master Food Preservers for a 90-minute class all about crafting your own fermented beverages at home. You’ll learn the basics of fermentation and dive into the art of making kombucha—from brewing your first batch to safely fermenting and flavoring it with fruits, herbs, and spices.

This hands-on workshop will guide you through each step, with plenty of tips to help you create delicious, bubbly kombucha tailored to your taste. Each participant will take home a starter kit to make their first batch at home with confidence.

This free class will be held at the Oceanside Public Library Mission Branch. Registration is required.

Come ready to sip, learn, and get brewing!

title: Womens Wellness Weekend
description: YMCA Camp Marston Women's Wellness Weekend 2026 Join us in the beautiful mountains of Julian at Camp Marston It's time to get ready for the YMCA of San Diego's annual Women's Wellness Weekend, happening September 11-13, 2026 . This weekend is the perfect opportunity to come together and celebrate the power of self-care and wellness among women. Whether you're a returning member or new to the YMCA, this weekend offers something for everyone. Get ready to be inspired, empowered and connected with yourself and others. Creating meaningful memories starts here! Please note: Registration is separate from your MY Y Account Portal. Please click below to create a profile or log in to CampInTouch. Secure Your Spot Today AREAS OF FOCUS Wellness Mindfulness Yoga Meditation Nutrition Friendship ACTIVITIES Relax and renew in a fun, supportive environment. Join classes focusing on strength, cardio and holistic mind/body wellness. Participate in classic camp activities like crafts, archery, hiking and campfires. Enjoy meals specifically prepared with your health and wellness in mind. LODGING YMCA Camp Marston offers 10 lodges that are 1700 square-foot each, 24 beds, 2 large bathrooms (four toilets, four showers, four sinks), forced air heat, a community living room with wood burning stove and four bunk rooms. Guests provide their own linens, toiletries and towels. Just bring a twin-size bottom sheet and sleeping bag/pillow for that true camping feel! MEALS As part of Women's Wellness Weekend, our focus is to provide a health-based menu for the weekend. Please note that vegetarian and gluten-free options are available. PRICING Pricing begins at $269/nonmembers (Up to 15% off with select Y memberships) CONTACT For questions or more information, please contact Sharnaye Neale, sneale@ymcasd.org.
location: Camp Marston, 4761 Pine Hills Rd, Julian, CA

title: Free Friday!
description: August Free Friday Activities 9am-12pm: Butterfly Information with Garden Butterfly Team and Numina Adrift (Bee Education) 9am-12pm: Heritage of the Americas Museum Open 9am–12pm: Gourd Demonstration with Terry 9am-1pm: SPECIAL: Vader Heirloom Seeds Tent (Shop heriloom seeds!) 10AM: Mini Tour with Garden Tour Team (Groups of 10 or more must call in advance to schedule a tour) 11:00 AM–12:00 PM: Storytime with Ms. Bee from Mother Earth Learning Center Registration required.
location: The Water Conservation Garden, 12122 Cuyamaca College Dr W, El Cajon, CA

title: Jimbo’s Garden Workshop: Playfully Mischievous Popcorn
description: Enjoy a special garden workshop in the Trudy Bronner Discovery Garden with local, seasonal ingredients from Jimbo's ! Today's recipe: Create p layfully mischievous popcorn inspired by Wicked with organic ingredients from Jimbo’s! Pre-registration is not required. FREE with Museum Admission.
location: Children's Museum of Discovery, 320 North Broadway, Escondido, CA

title: Lunch with a Raptor and Project Wildlife: Coexisting with Wildlife
partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
description: Join Project Wildlife for a brown-bag lunch info session with their amazing animal ambassadors! Raptors are found in all kinds of habitats on land — provided there is enough food! In addition to their striking appearance, they provide natural pest control, making them valuable neighbors to coexist with. Bring a lunch and a friend and learn all about Raptors and the their critical role in our ecosystem.
location: Grant Park, 2310 Camino Del Rio N., San Diego, CA

title: 3D Printer Drop-Off
description: Curious about how 3D printing works?  Drop off your creations at our computer lab where you can learn how to choose and print objects using our 3D printer.

title: Knot Together
description: Inspired by the traditional fishing nets and nautical knots featured in To Catch a Fish , our newest Together workshop series, Knot Together , explores the art of macramé. The series is led by Sitoë Thiam, a fiber artist and mechanical engineer who bridges technical precision with organic expression. As the founder of Unknot, a design studio specializing in knotting and weaving, she brings a unique interdisciplinary perspective to the world of fiber arts. Knotted Rope Wall Hanging In September, learn to transform rope into a sculptural wall hanging. You’ll explore four foundational knots, building a rhythmic, colorful composition that celebrates the tactile beauty of fiber. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , and Clay Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.
location: Mingei International Museum, 1439 El Prado, San Diego, CA

title: Tween Takeover: Paint and Sip a Rainbow Galaxy
description:
Event Details

It's Tween Takeover at the library!* Drop by the second Friday of the month for a tween takeover including but not limited to... crafts, snacks, flicks, games, and more! Each month Tween Takeover will change, so check in to see what is to come!

This Month...

Tween Paint and Sip class with Art Beat San Diego! For patrons ages 8-13*, come follow along with an instructor to paint a fun work of art and sip some sparkling apple cider. This month's painting will be shared soon!

Registration is required for this class. If you will not be attending, please cancel your registration to allow those on the waitlist to register.

*This program is heavily geared for kids aged 8-13, if your child is below this age the class will be challenging for them.

description: Learn about your San Elijo Lagoon – where migratory and resident birds share a sanctuary, and where many animals find a home.

title: Latino Conservation Week 2026
description: Get ready for San Diego’s 7th Annual Latino Conservation Week! A week of adventure, community, culture, and conservation is coming your way. Explore the coastal wetlands with Wander the Wetlands and Journey Through the Wetlands, experience the powerful Haagua FILM Screening & PANEL, celebrate our connection to the coast at the Beach Fiesta, and come together for our Latino Conservation Week Celebration. Whether you’re passionate about conservation or simply looking for new ways to enjoy the outdoors, there’s something for everyone. Bring your friends. Bring your family. Bring your love for the outdoors. Join us as we explore, celebrate, connect, and take action! RSVP at the link in bio or at https://bit.ly/LCWSD2026   Spanish ¡Prepárate para la 7.ª Semana Anual de Conservación Latina de San Diego! Se acerca una semana llena de aventura, comunidad, cultura y conservación. Explora los humedales costeros con Wander the Wetlands y Journey Through the Wetlands, disfruta de la poderosa proyección de la película Haagua FILM seguida de un panel, celebra nuestra conexión con la costa en la Beach Fiesta y únete a nuestra Celebración de la Semana de Conservación Latina.   Ya sea que te apasiona la conservación o simplemente buscas nuevas maneras de disfrutar del aire libre, ¡hay algo para todos! Trae a tus amistades. Trae a tu familia. Trae tu amor por la naturaleza.

title: Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour
description: Be an Ocean Connector and join us for a Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour! Join us for a guided Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour through the beautiful waterways of South San Diego Bay, ending in the restored Chula Vista Wetlands. This scenic, two-hour paddle offers a unique opportunity to explore coastal habitats while learning about the wildlife and conservation efforts that make South San Diego Bay so special. Along the way, you may spot osprey diving for fish, great blue herons and egrets wading in the shallows, nesting terns (April to September), and a variety of migrating birds (October to March). With a little luck, guests can even catch a glimpse of a Pacific green sea turtle cruising through the bay! This tour is welcoming to all skill levels and moves at a comfortable pace, with plenty of time to enjoy the surroundings. The route is about two hours long, and wind conditions can vary, adding a bit of adventure while still remaining accessible for beginners. What to Expect: Wildlife Viewing: Paddle through the waters, keeping an eye out for local wildlife, from native birds to coastal critters. Educational Insights: Our expert guides will provide fascinating information about the local ecosystems and conservation efforts. Chula Vista Wetlands: Paddle toward the restored wetlands, a vital area for wildlife and an important conservation success story. Come prepared for a fun and challenging adventure while experiencing the beauty of the Chula Vista Wetlands. Sign up for our next Wildlife Kayaking Eco Tour today! Best of all, every tour supports our education programs for South Bay youth! Find more information at www.oceanconnectors.org Group Discounts available on 6 or more tickets. Email eco-tours@oceanconnectors.org
location: Bayside Park, 999 Bayside Pkwy, Chula Vista

title: Latino Conservation Week: Wander the Wetlands & California Biodiversity Day
description: Join San Diego Bird Alliance and our partners for a fun, free, family-friendly morning celebrating the incredible biodiversity of Mission Bay's wetlands! Explore Kendall-Frost Marsh through hands-on activities and learn about the plants, animals, and habitats that make this ecosystem so special. San Diego Coastkeeper will lead a bilingual (English-Spanish) Water Quality Demonstration and provide insight into our latest 2025 Mission Bay Water Quality Report. This bilingual (English/Spanish) community event offers opportunities to connect with nature while contributing to community science during California Biodiversity Day. Activities include: Bird watching walk Fish seining demonstration Invertebrate exploration Native plant walk Nature observations with iNaturalist Water quality talk and demonstration Educational activities for all ages Whether you're an experienced naturalist or visiting the wetlands for the first time, everyone is welcome! Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026 Time: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM Location: UC San Diego Kendall-Frost Marsh (Crown Point Entrance) Come discover the amazing wildlife of Mission Bay and celebrate Latino Conservation Week and California Biodiversity Day with us! For questions, contact: Kornelas@sandiegobirdalliance.org Bring: Weather-appropriate attire and water Optional: Waterproof shoes and a camera We will meet at the southern end of Crown Point Park, near the dirt lot. Parking: San Diego, CA 92109 Address: Crown Point Dr, San Diego, CA 92109 Coordinates: 32°47'21.2″N 117°13'54.8″W Google Maps Link Register Here! Important Notes: Age: This event is suitable for all ages, though children must be accompanied by an adult. Accessibility: Please be aware that the terrain will include uneven sandy beaches. Expect to travel a short distance from the parking area to the meeting point and navigate uneven terrain, so be prepared for a bit of a trek. Weather Reminder: The event will take place rain or shine, but please check for updates in case of severe weather conditions. Safety: Please stay within the designated areas and respect the natural environment. Why Fish Seining? Fish play a critical role in maintaining the food web; they are an essential food source for many bird species. By monitoring fish populations through activities like fish seining, we can gain insight into the health of the marsh’s aquatic habitats. Healthy fish populations indicate clean, thriving waters, which ultimately benefit the birds that call the marsh home. In essence, by protecting the fish, we are also protecting the birds and the broader ecosystem. So, when you help us with fish seining, you’re not just learning about fish—you’re contributing to the long-term conservation of both the birds and the habitat they rely on. This is a partnership project between UC San Diego Natural Reserve System and San Diego Bird Alliance.

A bat researcher and scientist with Bat Conservation International Dan has more than 30 years of experience working on a wide range of wildlife and conservation issues in the U.S., Central America, and Africa. Dan has been with Bat Conservation Iternational for over 23 years and currently specializes in habitat protection and restoration. After our presentation we will stroll along the river, eavesdropping on the bats we see using our bioacoustics to identify them based on their calls. As the night concludes we will view the moths that have been attracted to our UV light station for up-close observation with Hector Valtierra. title: Latino Conservation Week “Journey Through the Wetlands” at Tijuana Slough
description: Celebrate Latino Conservation Week with a free, family-friendly event featuring bilingual nature walks, birdwatching, hands-on wetland activities, arts and crafts, and opportunities to connect with local conservation experts and community partners. Presented by San Diego Bird Alliance in collaboration with The Nat, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, the Hispanic Access Foundation, and local conservation partners, Latino Conservation Week is an annual celebration highlighting the important role the Latinx community plays in enjoying, protecting, and caring for our region’s natural resources. Participants can explore the wetlands through bilingual guided walks, birdwatching, nature talks, hands-on activities, arts and crafts, and interactive science experiences. From discovering the tiny creatures living in the water to learning about the plants and birds that depend on the estuary, there will be something for every age and interest. One of the highlights will be a hands-on experience in the estuary, where participants can help plant 50 native plants, take part in a water quality demonstration, and spend time with biologists. Local conservation experts will help participants understand what these activities reveal about the health and importance of our wetlands. Families can also explore local biodiversity using iNaturalist, connect with conservation organizations, and discover nature up close through specimens, microscopes, field guides, and other educational tools. Latino Conservation Week is more than a celebration of nature. It is a celebration of community, culture, and collective action. title: Community Science Plastic Pellet (Nurdle) Cleanup 9/19/26
description: Join us at Rotary Park in Carlsbad for a community science plastic pellet (nurdle) cleanup. Plastic pellets are the building blocks of the plastic supply chain, making so many of the products we use in our daily lives — everything from milk jugs to plastic bags. Unfortunately, they are also entering our environment at staggering rates, with more than 10 trillion plastic pellets entering our oceans annually. We are planning to continually monitor this site and collect data to address and quantify plastic pellet pollution in our communities and treasured waterways. The California coast has seen plastic pellet pollution in recent years, and the data collected through pellet counts paves the way for lasting change. This heart-centered session invites you to slow down, connect, and share in calming moments together with your little one. Gentle sound healing elements like soft crystal bowls, chimes, drum and gong sounds; create a soothing space for both you and your little one to relax and recharge. Sound healing can
support babies' sensory development, nervous system regulation, promote better sleep and emotional bonding. All caregivers welcome! Perfect for ages infants-2 but all children and adults are welcome.

Baby Storytime will resume it's normally scheduled programming on Monday, September 28th.

---------------------------------------------------------------

For this special takeover:

Dress comfortable
• Wear shoes that are easy to remove.
• Bring props (blankets, bolsters) to lie down comfortably
• Eat a light meal and hydrate beforehand.
• Listen to Your Body: If a sound is too loud or uncomfortable, it is okay to leave or move around.

Key Precautions & Contraindications
• Medical Devices: Those with pacemakers, defibrillators, or shunts should consult a doctor due to potential vibrational interference.
• Implants/Surgery: Metal pins, screws, or artificial joints might vibrate and cause discomfort. Post-surgical patients should wait.
• Pregnancy: Consult with and follow advise of medical professional/doctor
• Neurological Conditions: People with epilepsy or seizure disorders should exercise caution, as certain frequencies may trigger seizures.
• Mental Health: Individuals with severe, unstable mental health conditions or those prone to severe emotional triggers should consult a professional.
• Sound Sensitivity: Those with tinnitus or extreme sensitivities should use earplugs or sit further away from instruments.

description: Documentary Screening at the San Diego Air & Space Museum Friday, September 25, 2026 1:00 p.m. Pavilion of Flight Discover the remarkable story of one of aviation’s most accomplished—and often overlooked—pioneers during a special screening of The Flight of Jackie Cochran at the San Diego Air & Space Museum. The documentary will be presented on the Museum’s state-of-the-art LED video wall in the Pavilion of Flight. About the Documentary The Flight of Jackie Cochran tells the story of “the most famous pilot you’ve never heard of”—a woman who shattered aviation records, broke the sound barrier and helped change the course of history, only to be largely forgotten by it. A contemporary and rival of Amelia Earhart, Jackie Cochran became one of the most influential figures in American aviation. During World War II, she played a central role in establishing the Women Airforce Service Pilots, better known as the WASP, and later set an extraordinary number of speed, distance and altitude records. Behind Cochran’s public achievements, however, was a private life carefully constructed to conceal her past. Drawing on newly discovered archival materials and personal correspondence, the documentary explores a long-buried secret from her childhood and examines how her beginnings shaped her ambition, determination and relentless drive to succeed. The film also features scenes from the stage play The Flight of Jackie Cochran , written by and starring Nancy Hasty. Based on archival material uncovered during Hasty’s research, these dramatic reenactments bring Cochran’s voice and inner world to life while connecting her personal struggles with her historic accomplishments. More than a traditional biography, The Flight of Jackie Cochran examines how history chooses its heroes and why some extraordinary stories fade from public memory. It is a powerful exploration of ambition, perseverance, identity and the cost of greatness. Admission The screening is included with general Museum admission and is free for: San Diego Air & Space Museum Members Balboa Park Explorer Pass holders Seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

description: The Zoo Lady: The Forgotten Legend Who Saved & Then Built The San Diego Zoo She was a middle-aged, divorced mother who became the world’s first female zoo director and the first woman to lead the National Zoo Association (AZA)—so why has history forgotten her name? While Harry Wegeforth was the founder, it was Belle Benchley who ensured the San Diego Zoo survived its darkest days. In 1925, she took a temporary bookkeeping job at the struggling four-year-old zoo—a position she admittedly ‘dreaded’—only to stay for thirty years. She didn’t just save a failing institution; she built it into a world-class treasure, reshaping global conservation long before Jane Goodall or Dian Fossey. From wrestling rattlesnakes to orchestrating the historic cross-country giraffe trek that inspired the bestseller West with Giraffes, Benchley was a “leader of steel” who broke the glass ceiling. Join award-winning author and historian Dr. Sandra E. Bonura for a journey through rare archival images as she uncovers how this unlikely pioneer transformed a struggling local park into a global icon. description: LINDA HAWLEY’S NATURE ADVENTURES! FREE—ages 4-10 with an adult Not your ordinary sewer rats, woodrats are the original PACKRATS, building huge, intricate houses that last for centuries! Ms. Hawley has 40+ years of experience as a classroom teacher, college professor, naturalist guide & educator for Audubon Society’s OutdoorExplore! & at Mission Trails Regional Park, where she created & taught her “wildly popular” nature classes for 10 years. She is author of NATURE ADVENTURES! title: Skate Craft: Do-It-Yourself Design in Skateboarding
description: Celebrate skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, from the boards, gear, and ramps, to the machines and the repurposed boards as objects of use. To land a trick, to make the make—that moment is everything. It’s the struggle between you and the skateboard, the challenge of turning something sketchy into a clean run. Whether it's mastering a carve, dropping in, or landing a trick, the average number of attempts is 10,000. When you finally achieve it, that's when it becomes a true "MAKE." This exhibition celebrates skateboarding's true "Do It Yourself" ethos, tracing its evolution from the early days of making decks in garages and building ramps from found lumber to the handcrafted works of art seen today. Experience how skateboarding nurtures creativity, self-expression, and joy through artisanal craftsmanship. The progression of skateboard design, safety gear, and skate shoes, alongside the inventive machines that facilitated their creation, is driven by a DIY ethos. Around the world, artists embrace this spirit by turning old skateboards into jewelry and furniture, demonstrating how skateboarding combines play, design, and sustainability in vibrant ways.
